principles.statement: A plan created in one process must be readable, finalizable, and discardable by a later process — session stores are files, not memory.
principles.rationale: Live 2026-09-20: provisional plans (CreateProvisionalNodes) died with their process, so the finalize/rollback calls that needed them found nothing. A durable session store ({data_dir}/provisional/session_{id}.json) made the chain real, proven across fresh processes.

principles.statement: Finalization must record what became real (provisional id -> actual container id) in a durable place, not just return success.
principles.rationale: The materialization record is the correlation planning systems need; without it 'success' is unprovable after the fact and rollback has nothing to discard honestly.

principles.statement: Rollback must report exactly what it discarded.
principles.rationale: An honest rollback returns the discarded set — silence hides whether anything was ever at risk.

heuristics.name: Any plan/queue/draft state consumed by a later step or call.
heuristics.description: Persist at creation keyed by session id (filesystem-safe sanitized), record materializations durably, and make discard return what it discarded.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Provisional nodes, candidate queues, staged writes.

heuristics.name: Designing a multi-call workflow across process boundaries.
heuristics.description: Assume every call is a fresh process; the plan file is the only shared state, so its schema and location are the workflow's API.

decision_rules.action: Persist the plan durably before returning success; a step whose output dies with the process is not complete.
